tasks.short: Stop production when serious defects threaten product quality or safety.

steps.what: Review failed inspection results in the quality management system {OTHER}.
Inspect the affected process and establish the likely defect extent.
Order an immediate stop and define its production scope.
Halt the affected production equipment using its operating controls.
Place affected batches on hold in the {OPS_SYSTEM}.
Record the stop in the quality management system {OTHER}.
Notify planning and warehouse teams of the confirmed stop and holds.

tasks.design: A read-only evidence view joins inspection results from the quality management system {OTHER} to batch records in the {OPS_SYSTEM}. After the manager orders a stop and the supervisor confirms it, configured holds require batch-scope approval, while a deterministic template creates the incident record and sends containment notices through {EMAIL}. Physical stopping remains with trained staff using established operating controls.
tasks.previous_blocker: Defect evidence, batch identity and hold records sit in separate places. The serious-defect decision also depends on conditions at the line.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing hold configuration and modest integration code can connect these records. AI-assisted coding can reduce implementation effort, while established validation remains necessary.
tasks.still_hard: Tracing mixed or reworked batches and judging an unfamiliar defect remain difficult. Any change to equipment controls would need a separate engineering scope.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise an unsafe situation, challenge uncertain evidence and stop production despite delivery pressure.

ambition.what: Traceable containment status for production planning and warehouse teams

tasks.altitude: The manager spends less time copying stop details and answering status requests. Stop and restart authority remain unchanged; restart requires its own established release process.

reach.learn: Batch genealogy, stock status and the effect of a hold on downstream orders.

evidence.claim: Structured evidence views, batch-hold workflows and template reports can reduce administrative work around a human stop decision.
Physical containment and unfamiliar serious-defect assessment require site-specific operating knowledge and validation.

assumptions: The company has batch records, electronic inspection results and an existing hold function.
The manager has established stop authority; production staff perform the physical stop.
Time shares and build ranges are planning estimates for one site and one production interface.
Access work includes GDPR controls for identifiable incident records and employee consultation under national rules where applicable.
unknowns: Which defects require an immediate stop under the site's approved procedures?
Can the existing hold function cover split, mixed and reworked batches?
Which roles may stop production, confirm containment and authorise restart?
Are inspection and batch interfaces available with suitable access?
research_questions: Which sector-specific requirements govern electronic containment records and system validation?
new_work: Resolve missing or conflicting batch links.
Check failed hold writes and notification delivery.
Maintain defect thresholds, recipient lists and access permissions.
Periodically test the administrative workflow against containment procedures.

tasks.short: Review, revise and issue controlled operating procedures and quality manuals.

steps.what: Retrieve the current procedure and its linked change evidence from {DOCS}.
Compare the procedure with change evidence and identify affected sections.

loop.input: The controlled procedure and a fixed bundle of approved change evidence.
loop.output: Affected sections, proposed change reasons and source references.
loop.check: Verify source references and quoted text; the manager checks omissions and applicability.
loop.stop: At most two passes per procedure, with a 20-page input cap; larger or unresolved sections return to the manager.
loop.why_not_simpler: Changed operational meaning is expressed in prose and cannot be located reliably through field matching.

steps.what: Agree workable process changes with operators and the process owner.
Draft the revised procedure and its change summary.

loop.input: The current procedure, agreed change scope and cited evidence.
loop.output: A marked-up procedure draft and section-level change summary.
loop.check: Check template structure, preserved limits and source references; the manager checks technical instructions.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision per procedure; unsupported instructions are flagged for manual writing.
loop.why_not_simpler: Clear instructions must combine approved changes with existing prose; templates alone cannot express the changes.

steps.what: Approve the technical content, effective date and training requirements.
Publish the approved version and withdraw superseded copies in {DOCS}.
Assign required learning and acknowledgements in the {LMS}.

tasks.design: Configure version control, approval, publication and withdrawal in {DOCS}, with approved training requirements passed to {LMS}. Two bounded loops map change evidence to sections and draft revisions with source references; the manager and process owner settle operational changes before an authorised person approves publication.
tasks.previous_blocker: Document control can manage versions, but comparing narrative evidence and rewriting instructions still takes specialist attention. Links between incidents, procedure sections and learning assignments are often maintained manually.
tasks.enabler_now: Bounded language-model drafting can handle prose within an approved evidence bundle. Existing document workflows and faster integration development can connect release and training steps.
tasks.still_hard: Confirming that instructions work at the line, resolving conflicting requirements and withdrawing printed copies still require local effort.
tasks.human_edge: Translate process knowledge into instructions that operators can safely follow, and challenge changes that look sound only on paper.

ambition.what: Role-specific briefings for approved procedure changes

tasks.altitude: The manager spends more of the review cycle testing instructions with operators and less time assembling revisions. Approval rights remain unchanged; saved preparation time supports practical change briefings.

reach.learn: Document ownership, retention schedules and how to withdraw obsolete copies.

evidence.claim: Configured document workflows can enforce version status, approval and release conditions.
A bounded model loop can propose cited procedure revisions, while technical suitability still needs human review.

assumptions: Controlled procedures and change evidence are available as readable electronic documents.
The company already defines authorised approvers and training-assignment rules.
Time shares and build ranges are estimates for one procedure family and one release workflow.
Access work includes GDPR review of learning records and consultation under national rules where applicable.
unknowns: Does {DOCS} support controlled versions, withdrawal and approval records?
Who must approve each procedure family?
How many controlled paper copies exist?
Can approved role mappings drive assignments in the {LMS}?
What validation and retention requirements apply to these documents?
research_questions: Which sector-specific rules govern electronic approvals, document retention and proof of training?
new_work: Review draft changes and check omitted requirements.
Maintain evidence links, templates and drafting instructions.
Resolve failed publication or learning-assignment transfers.
Check that withdrawn copies disappear from operational use.

tasks.short: Monitor quality-system performance and decide where corrective or preventive action is needed.

steps.what: Export production volumes, rejects and inspection activity from the {OPS_SYSTEM}.
Export incidents and overdue actions from the quality management system {OTHER}.
Reconcile exports and calculate quality measures in a {SPREADSHEET}.
Review trends, exceptions and overdue controls in the performance report.
Investigate shortlisted issues with operators and process owners.
Agree improvement priorities, owners and completion dates.
Create assigned actions in the quality management system {OTHER}.

tasks.design: Scheduled jobs on {DATA_PLATFORM} join production data from {OPS_SYSTEM} with incidents and actions from the quality management system {OTHER}. Deterministic checks flag stale data, missing denominators and threshold breaches in {BI}; configured workflows create actions after the manager approves priorities.
tasks.previous_blocker: Production totals and quality records use different identifiers, dates and definitions. Manual reconciliation delays the report and hides data-quality problems.
tasks.enabler_now: Scheduled data pipelines, explicit metric definitions and dashboard tools already support this pattern. AI-assisted coding can shorten the work of building adapters and reconciliation checks.
tasks.still_hard: Changing product mix can distort apparent performance. Rare failures, weak denominators and underreported incidents still demand investigation.
tasks.human_edge: Distinguish a reporting artefact from a failing control, and secure operational changes without encouraging underreporting.
tasks.altitude: Routine reporting gives way to daily exception review and targeted floor investigations. A proposed delegation lets the manager reorder noncritical inspection work within approved sampling and release rules.

reach.task: Assess the cost of poor quality
reach.learn: Cost attribution, denominator selection and how product mix affects comparisons.

evidence.claim: Structured production and quality data support deterministic reconciliation, metric calculation and exception dashboards.
Metric changes alone do not establish root causes or prove that a quality control is effective.

assumptions: A quality analyst supports the manager; in smaller teams the manager performs those steps.
The current reporting bridge is a workbook assembled from operational exports.
Time shares and build ranges cover one site, two source systems and an agreed initial metric set.
The target uses process-level measures; identifiable records receive GDPR controls and any consultation required by national rules.
unknowns: Which metrics are already calculated reliably in existing systems?
Are production counts, rejects and incidents linked by stable identifiers?
Do records distinguish defects, rejected units, rework and repeat inspections?
Does the proposed inspection-priority delegation fit existing responsibilities?
Will any dashboard expose individual worker performance?
research_questions: Which statistical monitoring methods suit the relevant process distributions and production volumes?
If individual performance assessment is proposed, which GDPR, EU AI Act and national requirements apply?
new_work: Resolve data exceptions and late source records.
Maintain metric definitions and approved thresholds.
Check dashboard access and pipeline failures.
Review whether measures encourage missing or delayed incident reporting.

tasks.short: Review quality evidence for regulatory submissions and inspections.

steps.what: Confirm the submission or inspection scope and required evidence.
Retrieve controlled documents and records from {DOCS} and the quality management system {OTHER}.
Check required records, dates, signatures and versions against the evidence checklist.
Review whether the evidence supports required claims and identify contradictions.

loop.input: A fixed evidence bundle and the manager-approved requirement list.
loop.output: Proposed claim-to-evidence links, contradictions and unsupported claims with record references.
loop.check: Verify record identifiers, versions and quotations; the manager decides whether each claim is supported.
loop.stop: At most two passes and 20 records per checklist section; unresolved or larger sections go to manual review.
loop.why_not_simpler: Evidence sufficiency and contradictions depend on narrative meaning beyond metadata and checklist presence.

steps.what: Resolve evidence gaps with process owners and agree necessary corrections.
Approve the reviewed evidence pack or return it for further work.
Release the approved evidence pack to the regulatory team through {DOCS}.

tasks.design: A deterministic evidence builder gathers approved versions from {DOCS} and the quality management system {OTHER}, then checks required metadata and creates a traceable index. A bounded loop proposes claim-to-evidence links and contradictions for specialist review; {WORKFLOW} releases the pack internally only after approval, with external submission handled by the authorised regulatory role.
tasks.previous_blocker: Evidence retrieval and completeness checks span document stores and operational records. Substantive review depends on specialist interpretation, so assembly and judgement have remained intertwined.
tasks.enabler_now: Stable record references and deterministic checks can automate assembly. Bounded text comparison can prepare review findings without deciding regulatory acceptability.
tasks.still_hard: Selecting applicable requirements, assessing weak evidence and handling disputed records remain specialist work. Regulated environments may require substantial system validation.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise when apparently complete evidence does not substantiate a claim, and defend a candid account of unresolved gaps.

ambition.what: Pre-inspection evidence-readiness review for process owners

tasks.altitude: The manager spends less time locating files and more time challenging weak claims before inspection. Regulatory sign-off and external submission rights remain unchanged.

reach.learn: Evidence dependencies, approval lead times and how unresolved gaps affect the critical path.

evidence.claim: Record identifiers, version metadata and explicit checklists support deterministic evidence assembly and completeness checks.
A bounded model can prepare cited evidence findings, but specialist review is needed to assess regulatory sufficiency.

assumptions: The evidence scope is approved by a qualified person before automated retrieval.
Source records retain version history and can be referenced without overwriting originals.
Time shares and build ranges cover one evidence-pack type; extensive regulated-system qualification would expand the scope.
Access work includes GDPR review of personal data, confidential-record permissions and consultation under national rules where applicable.
unknowns: Which sector, regulator and submission types apply?
Who may approve evidence packs and submit them externally?
Are signatures, versions and retention metadata available electronically?
What personal or confidential information must be restricted or redacted?
Which validation procedures apply to changes in the evidence workflow?
research_questions: Which current sector rules define evidence admissibility, electronic signatures and retention?
What validation evidence is required for automated document retrieval and model-assisted review?
new_work: Review proposed evidence links and unsupported claims.
Maintain requirement mappings and completeness rules.
Handle unreadable records, conflicting versions and failed retrievals.
Retain source snapshots and review logs for reproducibility.
Revalidate affected workflow components when requirements or interfaces change.

role.altitude: The quality manager moves from assembling records towards investigating failures, testing procedures with operators and challenging evidence. Stop, release and regulatory approval responsibilities remain human; any added inspection-priority authority requires explicit delegation.
reach: Production planning: understand batch holds, genealogy and schedule consequences.
Administrative services: apply controlled-document practices to workplace procedures.
Management analysis: connect quality outcomes to credible cost measures.
Project management: coordinate evidence dependencies before inspections.
skills_to_grow: Define traceable quality metrics and recognise misleading denominators.
Specify deterministic checks, access controls and exception routes.
Review cited model drafts for omissions and unsupported claims.
Validate workflow changes against operational and regulatory requirements.
Facilitate practical procedure reviews with operators and process owners.
role.ambitious_version: Offer a shared quality-readiness service that gives process owners current containment status, focused procedure-change briefings and evidence-gap reviews before inspections.
